findings.title: parseBody after c.req.formData() fails or returns corrupted data
findings.why_it_matters: Any app where middleware or the handler calls `c.req.formData()` before `c.req.parseBody()` now breaks. For multipart requests parseBody throws `TypeError: Failed to parse body as FormData.` (an unhandled 500). For urlencoded requests it silently returns attacker-shaped garbage keys such as `{"------formdata-undici-...\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name": "\"foo\"..."}` instead of `{foo: 'bar'}`. The cause is that parseFormData now always calls `request.arrayBuffer()`. When only `formData` is cached, `#cachedBody` rebuilds the bytes with `new Response(formData).arrayBuffer()`, which re-serializes the data as multipart under a new boundary. Those bytes are then parsed against the original Content-Type (the old boundary, or urlencoded). Before this change parseBody called `request.formData()` and got the cached FormData back. The code also stores the rejected promise in `bodyCache.formData`, so later `c.req.formData()` calls fail too. This breaks the intent's promise not to regress c.req body-caching behavior. Reusing an existing `bodyCache.formData` first, as validator.ts already does, restores the old behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: In parseFormData, when `request instanceof HonoRequest && request.bodyCache.formData` is set, reuse the cached FormData: `formData = await request.bodyCache.formData`. This mirrors validator.ts:115-116. Only fall back to `arrayBuffer()` + `bufferToFormData` (and populate the cache) when no FormData is cached. Add a regression test that calls `c.req.formData()` and then `c.req.parseBody()` for both multipart and urlencoded bodies.
evidence: src/utils/body.ts:143 -- const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()
src/request.ts:228-235 -- const anyCachedKey = Object.keys(bodyCache)[0] ... return new Response(body)[key]()  (FormData re-serialized with a fresh multipart boundary)
src/utils/body.ts:144 -- bufferToFormData(arrayBuffer, headers.get('Content-Type') || '')  (parsed against the ORIGINAL boundary / urlencoded type)
src/utils/body.ts:147 -- request.bodyCache.formData = formDataPromise as unknown as FormData  (overwrites good cached FormData with the rejected promise)

Empirical (esbuild+node against HEAD): handler `await c.req.formData(); await c.req.parseBody()` -> multipart: 500 'TypeError: Failed to parse body as FormData.'; urlencoded: 200 {"------formdata-undici-097223617106
Content-Disposition: form-data; name":""foo"

bar
------formdata-undici-097223617106--
"}
Base behavior: `const formData = await (request as Request).formData()` -> HonoRequest.formData() -> #cachedBody('formData') returns the cached FormData directly

residual_risks: parseBody's form path now keeps the whole raw body in `bodyCache.arrayBuffer` and also holds the parsed FormData, so a request retains about 2x the body's memory for its lifetime, where the old native `formData()` held one copy. Only matters for apps that accept large bodies without the bodyLimit middleware.
testing_gaps: No test covers calling `c.req.formData()` before `c.req.parseBody()`, or `parseBody()` followed by `c.req.formData()`/`cloneRawRequest`, even though the new code changes which body cache key comes first (arrayBuffer now precedes formData).
